reason: Bank-health values to 2021 come from NBG's archive FSI file (quarterly, to 2023Q2) and values from 2022 from the current FSI file, which says it follows the 2019 FSI methodology. For 2022 the two files agree on capital, Tier 1 capital and return on assets, but give different values for bad loans (1.7% in the archive, 1.5% in the current file) and return on equity (30.2% against 24.8%). No change may be computed across this point for those two measures.
source_note: Archive FSI_Deposit_Takers_eng, 2022Q4 (Nonperforming loans by IMF's methodology 1.66%, Return on Equity 30.21%) against current FSD, December 2022 (1.51%, 24.79%). Archive note: "Calculated according to IMF methodology." Current file note: "Note: Data is calculated according to the 2019 FSI Methodology."

reason: The current FSI file says its data were reviewed from January 2023 because of the implementation of IFRS. In that file bad loans move from 1.51% in December 2022 to 3.10% in January 2023 (2.52% in December 2023). No change may be computed across this point.
source_note: Current FSI file, sheet FSD, cell B121: "Due to the implementation of the IFRS, data has been reviewed starting from 2023-01." Nonperforming loans to total gross loans, row 20: O20 (2022-12) 1.51%, P20 (2023-01) 3.10%.

reason: NBG says the changes in loans by type of economic activity since June 2014, compared with the months before, result from banks updating their clients' information about the client's economic activity. Part of an industry's change from May to June 2014 is therefore a move of existing loans between industries, not new lending. No change may be computed across this point for the industries.
source_note: L3.10.1 Total!B283: "Note: The structural changes of loans by type of economic activities since June 2014 compared with previous months are result of updating banks' clients' personal information regarding their economic activity."

reason: NBG includes overdue loan amounts in these figures from 1 December 2015. From the same month the L3.10.1 file gives Households and, inside them, Individuals and Individual entrepreneurs (its Households and Individual entrepreneur cells hold '...' and '-' before then); before it gives only Individuals (people). The household and purpose series start on the new basis. No change may be computed across this point for the series that run before it.
source_note: L3.10.1 Total!B284: "Including overdue loan amounts since December 1, 2015." LPR HH!A27: "Including overdue loan amounts since December 1, 2015."

reason: From September 2022 NBG sorts borrowers into sectors using the new unified register of legal entities, classifies economic activity by NACE Rev.2, and sizes businesses by the Eurostat method, which changed how business loans and loans to small and medium businesses are determined. NBG says the update did not change the total credit portfolio of legal entities. No change may be computed across this point for the series listed.
source_note: L3.10.1 Total!B285: "*** The unified database of legal entities registered in Georgia has been developed. Consequently, the categorization of institutional sectors has been updated from September 2022 . Also, the reports produced by National Bank of Georgia are presented with the updated classification of economic activity NACE.Rev2 from September 2022. In addition, the methodology developed by Eurostat for determining the size of the enterprise was introduced, which affected the targeting of business loans. Accordingly, from September 2022, the volumes of business loans and loans granted to small and medium businesses were determined by a new methodology. Mentioned classification update did not affect the volume of the total credit portfolio of legal entities." LPR HH!A28 carries the same note.

reason: NBG includes microbanks in all three loan tables from January 2025, so the 2025 values cover more lenders than the years before. This is a coverage change inside the series and is not adjusted. No change may be computed across this point.
source_note: L3.10.1 Total!B286: "The data have been updated to include microbanks from January 2025." LPR HH!A29 and LREG NC!A21 and FC!A21 carry the same sentence.
